anomalies.observed: On the schematic, the 20 k resistor R13 is connected between the tied MAX3485 DE/RE node (U2 pins 2 and 3, also Q3 collector) and NET0013, which is the same net that drives U2 pin 4 DI and the Q3 base resistor network. There is no pull-down of the DE/RE node to GND.
anomalies.expected: For the PNP-based auto-direction circuit described in the specification, the DE/RE node should be pulled to the idle-receive state (normally GND for this topology) so that Q3 can assert DE/RE only during transmit. The specification states: 'Q2 ... Auto TX/RX direction-control transistor: driven from /TXD2 ... to toggle the MAX3485 DE/RE enable pins.'

evidence.quote: U2 MAX3485 pins 2/3 tied together and to R13 20k; R13's other end is on NET0013, the same net connected to U2 pin 4 DI and Q3 base via R20.
Q2 | BC857 (PNP) | Auto TX/RX direction-control transistor: driven from /TXD2 (via R1 10k, R2 5.1k) to toggle the MAX3485 DE/RE enable pins.

anomalies.impact: With DE/RE pulled to TXD2 through R13, the tied DE//RE node remains high whenever TXD2 is high and is also pulled high by the PNP transistor when TXD2 is low. The MAX3485 driver would therefore be enabled and the receiver disabled continuously, preventing serial servo readback and potentially causing bus contention in serial mode.

parsed.summary: The likely anomaly is the MAX3485 direction-control network: the 20 k DE/RE resistor is tied to the TXD2/DI net instead of providing the required idle-low pull-down, which would keep the transceiver in transmit mode and break half-duplex serial operation.
